name: ApplicationContext vs BeanFactory
overview: Both Spring containers can wire beans. The interview gets interesting when one is wired wrong. Pick a container and predict when the failure shows up.

sections.title: Start with the container contract
sections.content: BeanFactory defines the core container contract for finding and providing beans. ApplicationContext builds on it with application-level services.

images.caption: ApplicationContext extends the basic bean factory contract with application services.

sections.title: Know when beans appear
sections.content: An application context typically creates non-lazy singletons during startup. A bean loaded on demand can surface a configuration issue later.

sections.title: Choose for the job
sections.content: Use ApplicationContext for a typical application that needs events, resource loading, messages, and automatic integration of container extensions.

keyPoints: Explain which container you'd choose for a typical Spring app and when a broken bean would fail during eager or lazy initialization.

references.title: Spring Framework Reference - Core Container (Beans, Context)

interviewQA.question: Why can ApplicationContext fail early?
interviewQA.answer: Default eager creation of non-lazy singletons can expose missing dependencies while the context starts.

interviewQA.question: What does ApplicationContext add?
interviewQA.answer: Application services such as event publication, message resolution, and resource access.
